title: Soccer Striker!
notes: Open Scratch at scratch.mit.edu and start a new blank project. Tell students that today they will make a game with a player, a soccer ball, a goalie, goals, a score, and a countdown timer.

title: Your mission today
notes: Ask students to predict which Scratch features each action needs: key sensing, loops, and variables. No code on this slide.

title: Build your soccer field
notes: The stage is the background. Sprites are game characters or objects that can move.

title: Wave goodbye to the Cat
notes: Students should start with a blank Scratch project. The uploaded reference project already has custom sprites; do not delete those if opening the finished file.

title: Paint your pitch
notes: Use a thick white brush. The stage in Scratch is 480 by 360 pixels. Keep the right edge clear enough for the Goal sprite.

title: Choose your Player
notes: Point out the sprite name text box below the stage. The name Player is important because Ball scripts will look for that exact sprite.

title: Start on the left
notes: Select Player. Snap the blue go-to block under the yellow event block. Show that negative x means left of center.

title: Face the goal
notes: Add both blocks under the Player flag stack. The Player looks right and fits on the pitch. Optional: set rotation style to left-right so the sprite does not flip upside down.

title: Keep checking!
notes: Snap forever underneath Player setup. Every arrow-key if block goes INSIDE forever. Do not put the forever beneath another forever.

title: Control your player
notes: Students already have a Player flag stack with a forever loop. These slides insert code inside that loop.

title: Right arrow → right
notes: Place an if block inside Player forever. Insert a Sensing key-pressed hexagon into the if. Put point direction 90 and move 5 inside.

title: Left arrow → left
notes: Add a NEW if below the right-arrow if inside forever, not inside the right-arrow if.

title: Up arrow → up
notes: Scratch directions are unusual: 0 = up, 90 = right, 180 = down, -90 = left. Students can write a compass on paper.

title: Down arrow → down
notes: Add the fourth separate if. Run game and press each arrow to debug directions.

title: Stay on the field
notes: Place this block at the bottom INSIDE Player forever, after the four arrow-key if blocks.

title: First play test
notes: Pause for one-minute student test. If controls do not work, confirm each if is inside forever and the code is on Player.

title: Make the ball move
notes: Students switch from Player to Ball. Different sprites have different scripts.

title: Add the soccer ball
notes: Exact sprite name must be Ball. In some versions, a Soccer Ball sprite may be available or students can paint a circle.

title: Set up the Ball
notes: Select Ball, not Player. Make a new green flag stack. Keep the score reset in this same flag stack later.

title: Only dribble when close
notes: Inside Ball forever, put if touching Player. Use light-blue Sensing block touching [Player]? (not touching mouse-pointer).

title: Copy the Player’s direction
notes: Critical: use Sensing reporter (x position of [Stage]) and change both dropdowns to direction of Player. Do not use Ball’s own direction bubble. This blue point block belongs inside the Ball touching Player if.

title: Give the Ball a push
notes: Add move 6 inside the Ball touching Player if, directly below point in direction of Player. Do NOT add repeat 16 here; the uploaded example file accidentally has an extra repeat and it should be removed.

title: Dribble test
notes: If ball teleports or flies: check there is no repeat 16 inside Ball dribble if; make sure direction of Player and move 6 are the only movement blocks in that branch.

title: Shoot and score
notes: Explain events and conditions: Space is an event; touching Player is the condition that allows a kick.

title: Paint the Goal
notes: Sprite must be Goal (capital G). Make its frame thick enough for collision detection. Make sure it is a sprite, not only painted on the backdrop, so touching Goal can work.

title: Space begins a kick
notes: On Ball, start a NEW stack, separate from the Ball green-flag forever stack.

title: You must reach the Ball
notes: Snap this condition under the space key event. Everything needed to kick goes INSIDE this if.

title: Aim at the Goal
notes: This Motion block appears inside the Space key touching Player condition. Confirm the Goal sprite is named Goal to appear in the dropdown.

title: Pop the Ball forward
notes: This is important. A small push might leave the Ball still touching Player, causing dribble code to interfere with the kick.

title: Make a powerful shot
notes: Put move 12 and wait 0.03 INSIDE repeat 16, which is inside the Space touching Player if, after move 60. A total possible shot distance is 60 + 16*12 = 252 Scratch steps.

title: First shot test
notes: Students may need to dribble past the halfway line first; the kick distance is intentional. If the ball leaps unexpectedly when walking, delete any repeat that was mistakenly placed in the dribble if.

title: Keep score
notes: A variable is a labeled number that can change during the game.

title: Make a Score variable
notes: Make Score available to all sprites. On the Stage in the supplied project, Score already exists.

title: Start at zero
notes: Insert this at the beginning of Ball’s green flag stack, before or after the starting Ball position.

title: Did it touch the Goal?
notes: Inside Ball forever add a SECOND if after the dribble if. The goal detection belongs in the Ball sprite, not Goal.

title: Give the Player a point
notes: Put both INSIDE the touching Goal if. The say block pauses that stack briefly.

title: First to 3 wins!
notes: Use green Operators = and orange Score variable bubble inside the smaller if. Put it below the Score+1 and GOAL announcement, inside the Goal touching branch.

title: Reset the Ball
notes: In the Ball touching Goal if, BELOW the win check, reset Ball and send a new ResetPlayer message. Students must choose New Message and name it ResetPlayer exactly.

title: Reset the Player
notes: Switch to Player to create this separate new stack. Test scoring twice and verify Score remains 2 and sprites reset after each goal.

title: Scoreboard check
notes: If score never changes, check touching Goal on Ball. If score increments multiple times, ensure Ball resets inside goal if. If the Player does not reset, check broadcast and receive spellings.

title: Add a goalkeeper
notes: Goalie uses an independent script, separate from Ball and Player.

title: Choose a Goalie
notes: Use position x=195, y=0, size 70%. Keep Goal behind Goalie. The provided sample project uses x 195.

title: Place your Goalie
notes: Select Goalie and create this setup. Size affects difficulty. You can also add show block to ensure the sprite appears after resets.

title: Patrol up and down
notes: Both glide blocks must be INSIDE Goalie forever. Uploaded project differs: it uses y ±50 and 2 sec; adjust for this lesson to y ±80 and 2.5 sec.

title: Check for a save
notes: Switch back to Ball. Add another if inside the Ball forever loop. The written lesson calls it the third if, after dribble and goal detection. If goal/save happen at exactly the same time, detection order may matter.

title: Saved!
notes: Put these two inside Ball touching Goalie if. The Player stays where they are on a save; only a GOAL broadcasts ResetPlayer.

title: Beat the clock
notes: This is a NEW flag-clicked stack on Ball. If students place this after forever in the same stack, the timer never starts.

title: Add the match clock
notes: Use a second all-sprites variable, Time. It should be separate from Score.

title: Start with 60 seconds
notes: Start a new Ball green flag stack for the clock. This is NOT below the Ball forever loop.

title: Keep going until zero
notes: Use Control repeat until, Operators <, and the Time variable bubble. The blocks on the next slide go INSIDE it.

title: Tick... tock...
notes: Place wait then change Time by -1 INSIDE repeat until. Students should be able to watch the number fall once per second.

title: Full time!
notes: These two blocks go AFTER repeat until, still in the new timer flag stack. If Score reaches 3 first, the win branch stops all scripts.

title: Kickoff! Play the game
notes: Ask each student to test a full match. Make sure pressing Space from far away does nothing, saved shots do not score, and Score resets when the green flag is clicked.

title: Bonus challenges
notes: All four challenges are optional extensions. They require more experimentation and are not needed for the base game.

title: Speed Boots
notes: Add a fifth if INSIDE Player forever. Extra move 4 steps is in addition to movement from the arrow key. Ask: why does the player sometimes outrun the ball?

title: Fix the fast dribble
notes: In the Ball touching Player branch, change move 6 to move 10. Compare 6 and 10 for how smooth the dribble feels. This changes normal dribbling too; a conditional speed boost is a more advanced fix.

title: Meet Player 2
notes: Duplicate Player, rename Player2, and give it a different costume color. Modify Player2 green flag starting position. Be sure reset code for Player2 is updated too.

title: WASD controls
notes: Duplicate the Player movement logic to Player2 and replace four arrows with W=up, A=left, S=down, D=right. Show this W example, then ask kids to make the other three.

title: Either player can dribble
notes: In Ball forever replace the touching Player condition with an Operators OR containing two Sensing touching blocks. The Ball needs extra logic to pick WHICH player’s direction; a simple direction-of-Player still follows Player1 even when Player2 touches. For the extension, add two separate dribble branches for each player or a direction selection if/else. Explain limitation clearly.

title: Player 2 can shoot
notes: Make a SECOND key stack on Ball for F. Continue by adding the same move 60 and repeat 16 → move 12 → wait 0.03 kick travel from Player 1, or the kick may fight dribbling. For truly competitive 2-player scoring, build a second Goal and separate scores; one Score variable only counts shared goals.

title: Slippery Ball
notes: Make a variable KickSpeed for Ball only. In the Space kick stack, replace the fixed repeat kick with a fading-speed loop. Note that preserving move 60 may be necessary to free the Ball from the Player.

title: Make the Ball slow down
notes: The move block uses the orange KickSpeed variable bubble instead of the number 12. It belongs inside repeat until.

title: Add friction
notes: Both blocks belong inside the same repeat until loop, after move KickSpeed steps. Ask children: how would changing -1 to -2 affect stopping distance?

title: Golden Goal
notes: Create a GoldenGoal variable; initialize to 0 at match start. On timeout, set it to 1 instead of immediately stopping. In a one-player game this is an overtime rule, not a true tie. A real two-player tie needs two scores.

title: Overtime begins
notes: In the time-up stack, remove stop all and display the Golden Goal message after setting GoldenGoal to 1. The existing win-at-3 code remains unless teacher chooses a different rule.

title: The next goal wins
notes: Put this inside Ball touching Goal branch after score updates. GoldenGoal must have been reset to 0 at the start of every match. This implements single-player overtime; two-player golden goal additionally needs team identification and separate scores.

title: You built a real game!
notes: Ask students to showcase one feature they built and one bug they fixed. Remind them to save the project with a memorable name and share it if their classroom settings permit.
